newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate eases 40 bps to 9.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate eases 40 bps to 9.7 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate eased 40 basis points to 9.7 percent on Friday, despite higher demand pushing up call money in a tight kuna market.
The weighted call money rate rose to 9.6 from 9.0 percent after some fresh loans were struck at up to 12 percent.
Trade totalled 21 million kuna, leaving a shortfall against the 26 million the banks sought partly to cover the week's turnover tax payment by their clients.
Lenders also rolled over 7.5 million kuna in loans maturing today at prices between 9.0 and 12 percent for term funds.
Because of an expected shortage in overnight supply, dealers said the central bank might also have to step in with Lombard loans at 11 percent to help banks square position.
Overnight trade is done at one percentage point below the average during the day.
The kuna mid-rates for Saturday and next Monday were weaker at 5.4963 and 3.5630 against the dollar and the German mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
